record.file_problem: None; the full post and comments are present. Some referenced figures and interactive material are not rendered in the supplied text.
record.tranche_reason: Compares SAEs across dictionary sizes and compares vanilla with a different training method, reporting results about feature preservation and absorption.
record.gate_note: The post reports results from its own toy model and TinyStories experiments. Results attributed to cited work are not included. The linked figures and interactive trees are not available as rendered evidence here.
record.test_reason: The post trains its own vanilla SAEs across widths (30 to 10k) on a TinyStories model and a hierarchical toy model, and reports absorption holes and fragmentation. It then compares a different objective (Matryoshka prefix losses) against same-L0 vanilla SAEs on the same question: whether splitting and absorption come from the training objective.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The author also argues absorption is likely an artifact of sparsity regularization and that fragmentation hides abstract structure the model likely uses. The abstract's claim that Matryoshka 'completely' avoids toy absorption is later qualified to most runs.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a summed loss over random SAE-latent prefixes, with periodic latent reordering, rather than simply comparing standard SAEs trained at increasing dictionary sizes. Both vanilla and Matryoshka variants use the post's log-sparsity loss.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported correlation advantage has exceptions at the residual stream before the first transformer block and the output of the first attention layer. Toy-model feature matching holds on most, not all, runs. Results are reported across L0 values 15, 30, and 60, but no per-L0 absorption outcomes are stated.
record.problems: The TinyStories model and SAEs have limited scale and training data, as the author notes. The text gives few numeric outcome values; linked plots and interactive material are not rendered. Toy-model matching is not reliable on every run. The author notes that some Matryoshka lower activations may be less interpretable and that the prefix sampling distribution was not optimized.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows for each reference SAE width or model location: the text reports the mean-maximum-correlation result in aggregate, with only two locations named as exceptions, and the linked graphs are not rendered. Comment-thread experiments by other commenters are not treated as results of the post's study.

record.verdict_notes: The reader linked the Matryoshka-vs-vanilla rows (r2–r5) to V1. They test V6, which explicitly names Matryoshka objectives. r9 is a method description. The Gemma-2-2B absorption results and chanind's narrow-SAE toy analysis come from commenters and are not the post's results. chanind's analysis would bear on V6, suggesting narrow SAEs also merge child features.

versions.untested_parts: Does not establish that every coarse feature is replaced by multiple finer features that partition the same inputs or lie near the coarse direction.
Large models and open SAE releases; experiments are on a 4-layer TinyStories model.
Does not establish that the identified latent families mirror a semantic hierarchy in the model's representations.
Does not systematically test whether changing dictionary size or sparsity alone fixes absorption.
No test of larger latents decomposing into combinations of smaller latents, novel latents, or whether any dictionary is complete and atomic.

Does not establish that SAE objectives generally explain splitting or that these results say little about model-internal units; tests the Matryoshka objective against vanilla SAEs in the reported settings.
